title: Finite local map surjective on cotangent spaces is surjective
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)\to(B,\mathfrak n,k)$ be a finite local homomorphism of local rings inducing the identity on the common residue field $k$ (a local homomorphism as in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]). If the induced map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ is surjective, then $A\to B$ is surjective. (Stacks Project, Algebra, Tag 0E8M.)

source.place: Tag 0E8M, lemma-when-surjective-local (its hypothesis that the maximal ideal of B is finitely generated is not needed: B/m_A B is Artinian local, so n = m_A B + n^2 forces n = m_A B, then Nakayama over A)

proof.text: Surjectivity of the induced map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ means that every element of $\mathfrak n$ is congruent modulo $\mathfrak n^2$ to the image of an element of $\mathfrak m$. Equivalently, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB+\mathfrak n^2$.

source.place: Tag 0E8M, lemma-when-surjective-local (translation of cotangent-space surjectivity into maximal-ideal generation)

proof.text: Set $\overline B=B/\mathfrak mB$ and $\overline{\mathfrak n}=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mB$. The quotient $\overline B$ is local with maximal ideal $\overline{\mathfrak n}$ and residue field $k$. Since $B$ is finite over $A$, $\overline B$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, so its ideal $\overline{\mathfrak n}$ is a finitely generated $\overline B$-module; moreover $\overline{\mathfrak n}$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of the local ring $\overline B$. The equality of Step 1 descends to $\overline{\mathfrak n}=\overline{\mathfrak n}^{2}$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] to $R=\overline B$, $I=\overline{\mathfrak n}$ and $M=\overline{\mathfrak n}$ gives $\overline{\mathfrak n}=0$, hence $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB$.

source.place: Tag 0E8M, lemma-when-surjective-local (quotient by mB and Nakayama applied to n/mB)

proof.text: Now $B/\mathfrak mB=B/\mathfrak n=k$ is generated over $k=A/\mathfrak m$ by the image of $1$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the local ring $A$, the finite $A$-module $B$, and the element $1\in B$, the element $1$ generates $B$ as an $A$-module. Thus the ring homomorphism $A\to B$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0E8M, lemma-when-surjective-local (final Nakayama application to the finite A-module B)
